ranking.why: The patient's echocardiography findings of markedly enlarged right atrium and right ventricle, along with tricuspid regurgitation, support this diagnosis, as stated in the Tricuspid Regurgitation reference material.

The patient's transesophageal echocardiography revealed a patent foramen ovale measuring 7.34 mm in width with a continuous, pure right-to-left shunt on colour flow mapping, which is consistent with the Patent Foramen Ovale reference material.
The patient's estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure of 55 mmHg and the presence of right atrial and ventricular enlargement are consistent with the Pulmonary Hypertension reference material.
The patient's history of cyanosis, exertional dyspnea, and the presence of a right-to-left shunt are consistent with the Eisenmenger Syndrome reference material.

The patient's pulmonary angiography showed no evidence of pulmonary embolism or pulmonary arteriovenous fistulae, which contradicts the Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension reference material.
The patient's symptoms and test results do not provide sufficient evidence to support or rule out this diagnosis, as stated in the Idiopathic Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension reference material.
